brief: The note reports a session driven by energy. Brent moved above $100/bbl for the first time since July after further US-Iran strikes, closing up 3.36% at $101.21, with the 6-month future at $86.09 as investors priced a longer period of high prices and doubted the Strait of Hormuz reopens soon. European gas futures closed up 4.49% at EUR79.25/MWh, the highest since 2022, after a fire at an industrial site in Russia's Yamalo-Nenets district and Ukrainian drone strikes on two gas condensate plants there. Higher energy prices fed faster hike pricing, with a September Fed hike moving from 61% to 63% and an extra 9.0bps of ECB hikes priced by June 2027, taking the total to 86bps. Yields rose, then accelerated after the Treasury confirmed buybacks of up to $6bn of longer-dated debt, short of some estimates: 10yr Treasury 4.84%, bund 3.44%, OAT 4.34%, UK 30yr 5.87%. Equities fell, S&P 500 down 0.48% for a third day with 404 decliners, STOXX 600 down 1.41%. Forward claims are the ECB preview, a 25bp hike expected today to 2.5% with no formal guidance, and DB's US data forecasts.
